title: Read a value off a graph or table
subtitle: One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread · 21 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **21 of the official questions in One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread are this one** — 18 Easy, 2 Medium, 1 Hard.
It is bottom-heavy, which makes it cheap points. Secure it early.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:

- You get a bar graph, dot plot, histogram, frequency table, category table or box plot, and the question asks for one count, a difference or sum of two counts, the category with a given frequency, the max or min value, or the median line of a box plot.
- No calculation beyond one addition or subtraction.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Find the exact row, bar or line the question names.
- 2) Read its height, frequency or position off the scale.
- 3) If asked, add or subtract the two readings.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: You only read a value off the display and maybe do one subtraction.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You read the wrong column of a frequency table, for example giving the largest frequency when the question wants the largest data value.
Or you take a box edge (Q1/Q3) instead of the middle line as the median.
Or you misread the gridline scale on a bar.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
